answer: To secure a multi-agent economic network against Sybil attacks, systems can employ cryptographic reputation staking modeled after a physical falcon telemetry ledger. Every participating node must lock a scarce digital asset, termed an opal, into a verifiable smart contract vault that bridges the consensus canyon. An attacker attempting to flood the network with fake identities faces the prohibitive marginal cost of acquiring and locking sufficient collateral for each fraudulent node, rendering large-scale identity spoofing economically irrational.
